content.text: I changed only `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (3 passed). The cause was operand order in the binary operations. The code popped the operands as `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which put the top of the stack in `a` and made it the left operand. That reversed `SUB`, `DIV`, `MOD`, `LT` and `GT`. So `1 2 LT` gave 0, dividing by zero checked the wrong operand and never raised `VMZeroDivision`, and the countdown loop's `SUB` computed `1 - x` and never reached zero. Swapping it to `b, a = pop(), pop()` makes `a` the second item down and `b` the top, so each operation computes `a op b`. I also fixed `SWAP`, which wasn't covered by a visible test but had a related bug: it pushed its two values back in their original order, so it did nothing. I checked it by hand afterwards: `1 2 SWAP` now gives `[2, 1]`, `7 2 DIV` gives `[3]`, and `7 2 MOD` gives `[1]`.

status_detail: fixed binary-op operand order and SWAP; 3 tests pass

result: I changed only `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (3 passed). The cause was operand order in the binary operations. The code popped the operands as `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which put the top of the stack in `a` and made it the left operand. That reversed `SUB`, `DIV`, `MOD`, `LT` and `GT`. So `1 2 LT` gave 0, dividing by zero checked the wrong operand and never raised `VMZeroDivision`, and the countdown loop's `SUB` computed `1 - x` and never reached zero. Swapping it to `b, a = pop(), pop()` makes `a` the second item down and `b` the top, so each operation computes `a op b`. I also fixed `SWAP`, which wasn't covered by a visible test but had a related bug: it pushed its two values back in their original order, so it did nothing. I checked it by hand afterwards: `1 2 SWAP` now gives `[2, 1]`, `7 2 DIV` gives `[3]`, and `7 2 MOD` gives `[1]`.
